title: add profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v17
author: Miguel Ramirez
release_notes: Adds v17 profiling baselines for representative workloads and wires benchmark-lab reporting into the new batch pipeline; no customer-facing API changes.
description: This PR adds the v17 profiling baselines for the benchmark lab representative workloads and integrates the reporting pipeline into the batch processing DAG. Motivation: recent model and runtime kernel changes changed tail-latency characteristics; we need new baselines to detect regressions and to feed the reporting dashboard. Changes include: 1) new baseline definitions and golden artifacts for Llama-3/Redwood-crit and open-variants; 2) a new reporting job that aggregates profiling traces, per-sequence latency histograms, KV-cache miss rates, and memory growth traces; 3) small runtime instrumentation hooks to tag requests with workload IDs; 4) CI benchmark job that runs representative workloads on canary infra and uploads artifacts to S3. Checklist: - [x] Add baseline definitions and golden outputs - [x] Add reporting DAG and job config - [x] Add e2e smoke for reporting upload - [x] Add docs note in benchmark-lab/README - [x] Add alert thresholds for deviations. This is a non-breaking changeset and should be low-risk; most work is additive and behind feature flags.
commits: Add v17 profiling baselines and golden artifacts
Add reporting DAG and batch job for benchmark lab
Add CI job for benchmark reporting and S3 uploader
diff_snippets: + 'workload_id' added to request metadata in instrumentation/workload_tagging.go
+ New DAG reporting_v17.py schedules nightly aggregation and uploads to S3
+ baseline golden JSONs added under benchmark-lab/baselines/v17
review_comments: Lina Chen: Can you clarify how the workload_id is generated for multi-tenant runs? Miguel: workload_id is derived from the workload runner config (bench_id + seed) and passed through the request metadata; added a short note in instrumentation/README.

Asha Patel: The new reporting CI job uploads artifacts to a shared S3 bucket; what access controls are in place? Miguel: The CI job assumes role benchmark-ci-uploader with limited PutObject permissions; added a note in reporting-ci.yml and a follow-up task to rotate credentials monthly (linked ENG-2950).

Jonas Becker: Observability changes look good but we should avoid expensive hist aggregation in the hot path. Miguel: moved histogram bucketing to the batch job and left only counters in the runtime; updated aggregate_profile.py to do offline bucketing.

Lina Chen (follow-up): Can we add a smoke test to assert the DAG completes successfully on canary? Miguel: added a minimal e2e smoke that runs one representative workload in redwood-ci/benchmarks/reporting-ci.yml.
ci_notes: integration-tests initially flaky on 2025-02-20 due to transient S3 permissions; re-run fixed the job
benchmark-ci runs nightly on canary infra and attached artifacts to the PR
notes: Follow-up work: ENG-2950 (credential rotation), ENG-3033 (add tiered baselines for dedicated capacity), and a small perf tweak planned to reduce peak memory during profiling runs.
changelog_entry: benchmark: add profiling baselines v17 and reporting pipeline integration
docs_changes: benchmark-lab/README.md: updated reporting and CI instructions
testing_instructions: Run redwood-ci/benchmarks/reporting-ci.yml pipeline or execute perf-canary/jobs/run_representative_workloads.sh with --upload to reproduce reporting artifacts and verify aggregation on S3.
risk_assessment: low: additive reporting and offline aggregation reduce risk. Runtime tagging is lightweight and gated behind a feature flag for rollout.
